de.title: Englische Redewendungen 2: the ball is in your court und mehr
de.intro: Vier englische Redewendungen aus dem Arbeitsalltag, mit Bedeutung und Beispielsatz.

cards.front: the ball is in your court
cards.back: Du bist am Zug, du musst jetzt handeln oder entscheiden. I've sent you my offer, so the ball is in your court.
bei einer Arbeit unsauber vorgehen oder unzulässig abkürzen. The builder cut corners, and the wall cracked within a year.

cards.front: to be on the same page
cards.back: sich einig sein, dasselbe Verständnis haben. After the call, our team was finally on the same page about the schedule.
wieder am Anfang stehen, nach einem Fehlschlag oder einer Sackgasse. The test failed, so we're back to square one.

cards.front: Woher stammt "the ball is in your court"?
cards.back: Aus dem Tennis: Wer den Ball in seinem Feld hat, ist am Zug.

cards.front: Woher stammt wohl "back to square one"?
cards.back: Vermutlich aus dem Brettspiel Schlangen und Leitern.

cards.front: Welche deutsche Wendung passt zu "the ball is in your court"?
Welche ähnlichen Wendungen gibt es zu "on the same page"?
cards.back: on board und to see eye to eye

en.title: English Idioms 2: the ball is in your court and more
en.intro: Four English idioms from everyday work, with meaning and an example sentence.

cards.front: the ball is in your court
cards.back: It's your turn to act or decide. I've sent you my offer, so the ball is in your court.
to do a job sloppily or take improper shortcuts. The builder cut corners, and the wall cracked within a year.

cards.front: to be on the same page
cards.back: to be in agreement and share the same understanding. After the call, our team was finally on the same page about the schedule.
back at the start after a failure or dead end. The test failed, so we're back to square one.

cards.front: Where does "the ball is in your court" come from?
cards.back: From tennis: whoever has the ball in their court is the one to play.

cards.front: Where does "back to square one" probably come from?
cards.back: Probably from the board game snakes and ladders.

cards.front: Which German phrase matches "the ball is in your court"?
Which similar phrases exist for "on the same page"?
cards.back: on board and to see eye to eye
